feature: One Curve row for every transition
summary: Everything that moves from one state to another over time now has the same Curve row in the panel, right under its length: a zoom's way in and out, a transition at a cut, a clip or title's Fade In and Fade Out, a sound's fades and the stretch between two keys (which is how Animate In and Out work). Each offers the same eight named curves, Draw a Curve, and any curve you drew and saved by name.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default. Open the sample recording with the timeline showing.
inventory: Zoom way in and way out: Ease In and Ease Out lengths (were the only control; the curve was fixed smootherstep). Now also Curve, one for both, or Curve In and Curve Out set apart. Default Smooth, the curve zooms always used.

Transition at a cut, inside one clip or between two clips (dissolve, dips, push, wipe, blur through): Type, Length, overlap side, Hold on black (ran straight, no curve). Now also Curve, default Linear. A dip runs the curve on each half, so it is all colour on the cut whatever the curve.

Fade In and Fade Out on a clip, title, shape or component (Time section): lengths only, ran straight. Now also Curve (shown once there is a fade), default Linear; the fade wedge on the clip bar is drawn along the curve.

Title and name card Animate In and Out (right click): writes keys, so its curve is the Between the keys Curve row in Properties, which already took the shared list. Now on the shared row, with Saved curves.
Keys in general (Between the keys): already had the shared list. Now on the shared row, with Saved curves.
Sound Fade In and Fade Out (Audio fades): already had the shared list. Now on the shared row, with Saved curves.
Not changed: the sound under a transition keeps its constant-power cross-fade, and a dip's Hold on black has no curve (it is a hold, not a change).
measured: Zoom, 1.5s way in on the drawn curve Slow start: canvas 2.0% / 10.0% / 30.6% in at 25 / 50 / 75%, curve 2.0% / 10.0% / 30.6%. Way out 98.0 / 90.0 / 69.4 against 98.0 / 90.0 / 69.4. The canvas matched the exported frame at a quarter, half and three quarters of the way in (0.0% of pixels apart).
Cross dissolve, 1.0s on Slow start: incoming shot 2.0% / 10.0% / 30.6% up at 25 / 50 / 75%, the same on the canvas and in the frame the exporter draws, curve 2.0% / 10.0% / 30.6%.

Unit tests check every named curve and a drawn one on a zoom's way in and out, a dissolve, a dip's two halves, a dissolve between two clips and a picture fade, within 2% at a quarter, a half and three quarters.

evaluate: Is the Curve row where you expect it each time, right under the length it shapes?
Does a dip that eases, still all black on the cut, feel better than one that runs straight?
Is Set In and Out Apart, inside the zoom's Curve menu, a place you would find it?
Should saved curves be listed under Saved in every Curve menu, or only where you saved them?
Is Smooth, offered only on zooms, the right name for how zooms have always moved?
rough: No mock covers a Curve row on a zoom, a transition at a cut or a picture fade; the app goes further than the transition mock (video-transition-wt.html, #propsCut), which stops at Type, Length, Paid with and the overlap. Curve sits right under Length, as it does under the zoom's eases and the fades.
The Curve menu matches the key curve mock (curve.js): Standard four, Shaped four, each with its shape, then Draw a Curve. Saved and Forget are additions after the eight.

A zoom's default, Smooth, is not one of the shared eight: zooms have always eased on it, and keeping it is what lets old documents play exactly as before. It shows at the end of the Shaped curves on zooms only.

A clip with a fade and a sound shows two Curve rows, one under Fade In and Fade Out (Time) and one under Audio fades, and a title with keys and a fade shows Between the keys Curve and the Time Curve: each sits under the thing it shapes.
Title Animate In and Out have no Length row of their own: their length is the distance between the keys, dragged on the timeline.
The sound under a transition does not follow the curve; it keeps the constant-power cross-fade an editor expects. Only the picture is shaped.
The walk stands in for dragging the two handles in Draw a Curve (it sets the drawn curve and saves it the way Save does); the handles themselves are the existing curve editor's, not new.
The zoom bar on the timeline does not draw its curve; the fade wedge on a clip bar does.
